answer: Anchor each identity to a blood-donation record. A donor registers once with a blood bank, which verifies ID and blood type and issues a jade-green donor card bound to a public key. Each epoch the donor visits the clinic inlet and gives a fresh sample; the bank signs a receipt for that week's donation, sealed under a rotating cipher keyed to the epoch nonce so old receipts cannot replay. A farm wanting one hundred votes needs one hundred real donors giving real blood; shared donors collapse to one vote and forged receipts burn the bond. An honest person donates once and keeps their vote.
